intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to give your own opinion (〜と思います) and to report what someone else said, either word for word or in summary (〜と言います). You will also meet でしょう？ for asking 'isn’t it?' to get agreement, 〜で〜があります for saying where an event takes place, について for 'about', and 〜ので for giving a reason softly. Because Japanese と works just like Tamil 'என்று' (that / saying), this lesson should feel very easy for you.

g21-1.explanation_en: Use 〜と思います to give your opinion or a guess. In Tamil, when you say 'நாளை மழை பெய்யும் என்று நினைக்கிறேன்' (I think it will rain tomorrow), the order is full sentence + 'என்று' + 'நினைக்கிறேன்', right? Japanese uses exactly the same order: sentence + と + 思います. Here と is Tamil 'என்று'. The sentence before と must be in the plain form (普通形) you learned in Lesson 20: 降る、降らない、降った、難しい、難しかった. Nouns and な-adjectives take だ: 先生だと思います、大切だと思います. To say 'I don’t think so', you can use either 〜ないと思います (negative inside) or 〜とは思いません (negative outside); for N5 the first way is enough. To ask someone’s opinion, say 〜についてどう思いますか.
g21-1.tamil_parallel_en: நாளை மழை பெய்யும் என்று நினைக்கிறேன் (I think it will rain tomorrow) = 明日は雨が降ると思います. The order is the same in both languages: sentence + என்று (と) + நினைக்கிறேன் (思います).
g21-1.formation_en: V / い-adj plain + と 思います ； N / な-adj + だ + と 思います ； Negative: 〜ない + と 思います
g21-1.pitfalls_en: A common mistake is putting the ます-form before と: ×降りますと思います → ○降ると思います. Don’t forget だ after a noun: ×先生と思います → ○先生だと思います.

g21-2.explanation_en: Use 言います (to say) to report what someone said. There are two ways. (1) Direct speech: put the exact words inside 「 」 and add と言いました: 田中さんは「おはよう」と言いました. (2) Indirect speech: give the meaning of what was said in plain form and add と言いました: 先生は明日テストがあると言いました. Here too, と = Tamil 'என்று', just like we say in Tamil 'அவர் நாளை தேர்வு இருக்கிறது என்று சொன்னார்' (he said there is a test tomorrow). To ask 'How do you say X in Japanese?', use 「X」は日本語で何と言いますか. When you pass on what someone said, you can also use 言っていました (was saying / had said).
g21-2.tamil_parallel_en: ஆசிரியர் 'நாளை தேர்வு' என்று சொன்னார் (the teacher said 'test tomorrow') = 先生は「明日テストです」と言いました. Tamil என்று and Japanese と both link the quoted words to the verb 'say'.
g21-2.formation_en: 「direct speech」 + と 言います ； plain form + と 言います ； 「X」は 〜語で 何と 言いますか
g21-2.pitfalls_en: The speaker of 言います is marked with は, and the person spoken to is marked with に: 田中さんは私に…と言いました. Don’t confuse 言う with 話す (to talk): と does not come before 話す.

g21-3.explanation_en: Use でしょう？ (with rising intonation) to confirm something when you expect the listener to agree: 'isn’t it?' / 'right?'. It matches Tamil 'இந்தச் சாப்பாடு சுவையாக இருக்கிறது, இல்லையா?' (this food is tasty, isn’t it?) or 'நீ நாளை வருவாய்தானே?' (you’re coming tomorrow, right?). The plain form comes before でしょう; nouns and な-adjectives do not take だ: 日本人でしょう？、静かでしょう？. Like ね from Lesson 4, it asks for agreement, but でしょう fits especially well when you ask about something the listener already knows.
g21-3.tamil_parallel_en: இந்தச் சாப்பாடு சுவையாக இருக்கிறது, இல்லையா? (this food is tasty, isn’t it?) = この料理、おいしいでしょう？ The Tamil tag இல்லையா? / -தானே? does the same job as でしょう？.
g21-3.formation_en: V plain / い-adj plain + でしょう？ ； N / な-adj (without だ) + でしょう？
g21-3.pitfalls_en: Don’t put だ after a noun: ×日本人だでしょう → ○日本人でしょう. If you say でしょう with falling intonation, it becomes a guess, 'it is probably so'; to ask for agreement you need rising intonation.

g21-4.explanation_en: In Lesson 10 we marked the place where a thing exists with に, as in 'there is a book on the desk' (机の上に本があります). But for events such as a party, test, class or festival, the place where the event 'happens' is marked with で: 学校でパーティーがあります. It is like Tamil 'பள்ளியில் பார்ட்டி இருக்கிறது/நடக்கிறது' (there is / will be a party at school). Why で? As you learned in Lesson 6, で marks the place where an action happens, and an event is an action, so it takes で. The time of the event comes first with に: 土曜日に学校でパーティーがあります.
g21-4.tamil_parallel_en: சனிக்கிழமை பள்ளியில் பார்ட்டி இருக்கிறது (there is a party at school on Saturday) = 土曜日に学校でパーティーがあります. Place + -இல் (で) + event + が + あります.
g21-4.formation_en: N(time) に + N(place) で + N(event) が あります ； Negative: 〜が ありません
g21-4.pitfalls_en: Using に for events is a common mistake for Tamil speakers, because in Tamil both are '-இல்' (in/at): ×学校にパーティーがあります → ○学校でパーティーがあります. Only the place where a thing exists takes に.

g21-5.explanation_en: To say what you talk, write or think 'about', add について after the noun. It is a direct match for Tamil '-ஐப் பற்றி' (about): 日本の食べ物について (ஜப்பானிய உணவைப் பற்றி, about Japanese food). You can remember について as one word; nothing like の or を comes before it. It is usually followed by verbs such as 話します、書きます、質問があります、どう思いますか. To describe a noun with 'about' (a book about...), use についての N: 日本についての本.
g21-5.tamil_parallel_en: பயணத்தைப் பற்றி நண்பனுடன் பேசினேன் (I talked with my friend about the trip) = 旅行について友達と話しました. N + பற்றி (about) = N + について.
g21-5.formation_en: N + について + V (話します / 書きます / 聞きます / 思います)
g21-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t put を before について: ×旅行をについて → ○旅行について. Using only に for 'about' is also wrong.

g21-6.explanation_en: After one sentence ends, you can start the next one with 'but' using でも or しかし. It is like Tamil 'ஜப்பானிய மொழி கடினம். ஆனால் சுவாரசியமானது.' (Japanese is hard. But it is interesting.). でも is used in spoken language, with friends and in everyday talk; しかし is used in essays, news and formal speech. Both stand alone at the start of a sentence, followed by 、. The difference from 〜が、〜 (Lesson 8) and 〜けど (Lesson 20) is that those attach to the end of the previous sentence, while でも/しかし begin a new sentence.
g21-6.tamil_parallel_en: இந்தக் கடை விலை அதிகம். ஆனால் சுவையாக இருக்கும். (This shop is expensive. But it is tasty.) = この店は高いです。でも、おいしいです。 Tamil ஆனால் (but) at the start of the second sentence matches でも / しかし.
g21-6.formation_en: Sentence 1。 + でも、 / しかし、 + Sentence 2。
g21-6.pitfalls_en: Don’t put でも in the middle of a sentence to mean 'but': ×高いですでも、 → ○高いですが、 or ○高いです。でも、.

g21-7.explanation_en: In Lesson 9 you learned 〜から for giving a reason. 〜ので does the same job, but it sounds softer and more polite; it presents the reason as a natural cause: 'because of this, that happened'. It matches Tamil '-ஆதலால்', '-என்பதால்' (because / since): 時間がないので (நேரம் இல்லாததால், because there is no time). The plain form comes before ので; nouns and な-adjectives become なので: 風邪なので、下手なので. Using ので when you apologise, refuse or make a request is more polite. Before から the ます/です form can also come, but before ので the plain form is normally used.
g21-7.tamil_parallel_en: நேரம் இல்லாததால் டாக்ஸியில் போகிறேன் (because there is no time, I will go by taxi) = 時間がないので、タクシーで行きます. Reason + -ஆதலால் (ので) + result, in the same order as Tamil.
g21-7.formation_en: V / い-adj plain + ので、〜 ； N / な-adj + なので、〜
g21-7.pitfalls_en: Saying だので after a noun is wrong: ×風邪だので → ○風邪なので. A request like 'please do' can follow ので, but for an invitation like 'let’s do' (ましょう), から fits better.

items.L21-q01: 新聞 = しんぶん (செய்தித்தாள், newspaper). Here 聞 is read ぶん, not the きく reading of 聞く (to listen). しんもん is a trap that mixes it up with 質問 (しつもん).
items.L21-q02: 声 = こえ (குரல், voice). ごえ is the voiced change (こ→ご) that only happens inside compounds; on its own the word is always こえ. おと is a different word meaning 'sound'.
items.L21-q03: 言葉 = ことば (வார்த்தை, word). Here 葉 is voiced as ば; saying ことは without the voicing is wrong. In こどば the と has wrongly become voiced.
items.L21-q04: おなじ = 同じ (ஒரே, same). 回 (かい, time/occurrence) and 国 (くに, country) are kanji that look like 同; 同 has one line and a 口 inside.
items.L21-q05: しつもん = 質問 (கேள்வி, question). 問 (もん) has a 口 inside; 門 (gate) has no 口 inside, and that is the trap in 質門. 貿 and 資 are different kanji that look similar to 質.
items.L21-q06: To politely refuse with 'no thanks, that’s enough', people say いいえ、結構です (けっこうです) (வேண்டாம், போதும், no thank you). べんり (convenient) and たいせつ (important) don’t fit here.
items.L21-q07: To say 'A is different from B', use AはBと違います (வேறுபடுகிறது, is different). 答えます (to answer) and 始まります (to begin) don’t fit the meaning here.
items.L21-q08: 大勢の人 = (நிறையப் பேர், a lot of people). 大切 (important), 大変 (hard/tough) and 大丈夫 (all right) are other words that start with 大; only 大勢 refers to a number of people.
items.L21-q09: It 'starts' at nine (始まります, தொடங்குகிறது) and ends at twelve. 止まります (stops) is for a vehicle or machine stopping, not for a class.
items.L21-q10: To ask 'why didn’t you come', use なぜ (ஏன், why) (= どうして). If you asked いつ (when), it wouldn’t fit, because the answer 昨日 (yesterday) is already in the sentence.
items.L21-q11: What you 'watch' on TV is ニュース (செய்தி, news). ラジオ is something you listen to; besides, you can’t watch the radio on TV. 声 (voice) is also something you hear.
items.L21-q12: 'A student at the same school' means both of them study at one school. The first option (違います = is different) means the exact opposite; 先生 (teacher) is not a student.
items.L21-q13: Direct speech 「明日休みます」 (I will take tomorrow off) = indirect speech 明日来ないと言いました (நாளை வர மாட்டேன் என்று சொன்னார், he said he won’t come tomorrow). 来る/働く give the opposite meaning; 昨日 is the wrong time.
items.L21-q14: 'I don’t understand the meaning' = 'I don’t know this word' (知りません, தெரியாது). 難しくない (not difficult) is the opposite meaning; using it often (よく使います) doesn’t fit a word you don’t know.
items.L21-q15: The plain form (普通形) must come before と思います: 降ると思います (பெய்யும் என்று நினைக்கிறேன், I think it will fall). Putting the ます-form (降ります) there is a common mistake for Tamil learners.
items.L21-q16: With noun + と思います, you need だ in between: 先生だと思います. です is the polite form and doesn’t come before と. な is only used when a な-adjective describes a noun.
items.L21-q17: To link what was said to 言いました, use と (= Tamil 'என்று'). Using を is the trap of translating Tamil '-ஐ' in 'சொன்னதை' (what was said) directly.
items.L21-q18: Noun + ので becomes なので: 風邪なので (சளி என்பதால், because I have a cold). だので does not exist. To use から it would have to be 風邪ですから / 風邪だから; 風邪から alone changes the meaning to 'from a cold'.
items.L21-q19: A party is an event, and the place where an event happens takes で. に is only for the place where a thing exists (公園に木があります).
items.L21-q20: 'About' = について (பற்றி), as one word. Adding を or の to make をついて/のついて is wrong.
items.L21-q21: Plain form 行く + でしょう？ = (போகிறீர்கள்தானே?, you’re going, right?). 行くですか is a wrong combination (it should be 行きますか); forms like 行くません/行くましょう don’t exist.
items.L21-q22: 田中さんは パーティーに 来ないと 思います。 — (தனாகா பார்ட்டிக்கு வர மாட்டார் என்று நினைக்கிறேன், I think Tanaka won’t come to the party). The order is plain negative 来ない + と + 思います; 来ない goes in the star position.
items.L21-q23: 明日 学校で 日本語の テストが あります。 — The place where the event happens (で) comes first, then 'which test' (日本語の テストが), and あります at the end. テストが goes in the star position.
items.L21-q24: 時間が ないので、駅まで タクシーで 行きます。 — The reason (ないので) comes first, then 'as far as where' (駅まで), 'by what' (タクシーで), and the verb at the end. タクシーで goes in the star position.
items.L21-q25: ［1］ After direct speech, use と to link it to 言いました. ［2］ My friend said it is 'difficult', but I think it is 'not difficult': an opposite opinion, so でも (ஆனால், but); そして/それから mean 'and then', a continuation. ［3］ The plain form 行く must come before と思います; 行きます is wrong.
